source_row.rationale: ACE inhibitor-induced angioedema is a rare but potentially life-threatening adverse effect, distinct from the more common ACE inhibitor cough, involving rapid swelling of the lips, tongue, face, or airway due to bradykinin accumulation. This requires immediate discontinuation of the medication, airway assessment, and emergency intervention if airway compromise is present, since it can be fatal if untreated.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed lisinopril labeling, Warnings and Precautions 5.2 Angioedema: promptly discontinue; tongue/glottis/larynx involvement may cause airway obstruction and require emergency therapy. Current FDA/DailyMed label reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
